## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

# Corporate Title Renaming — All 45 Agents

## Context

The current org chart uses internal-jargon titles ("VP Engineering", "Pod A Lead", "Stack A Backend", "Public-Facing Page Designer") that don't read like a real company org. The user wants every agent to have a clean, corporate-sounding job title — the kind you'd see on LinkedIn at a real software company — so the chart feels like a real employee team, not an internal taxonomy.

**Specifically broken:**
- "VP Engineering / VP Growth / VP Research / VP Creative" — too generic, not differentiated, doesn't scale.
- "Pod A Lead / Pod B Lead / Pod C Lead" — meaningless without insider context.
- "Stack A Backend / Stack B Backend" — engineering jargon leaking into titles.
- "Public-Facing Page Designer", "Idea Validator", "Bug Fixer" — descriptive but not job-title-shaped.

**Outcome:** Every agent gets a recognisable corporate title (C-suite for top layer, Head of / Director of for second layer, Senior X / Lead X / X Engineer for ICs). Pods get human-readable team names. Org chart reads like a real company.

---

## Naming Framework

Three tiers, applied consistently:

| Tier | Pattern | Examples |
|------|---------|----------|
| **Top of dept (7)** | Chief X Officer | CEO, CTO, CDO, CMO, CGO, CRO, CPO |
| **Sub-dept lead** | Head of X / Director of X | Head of SEO, Director of CRO |
| **Pod / team lead** | Engineering Manager — *Team* | Engineering Manager — Web Platform |
| **Senior IC** | Senior X / Principal X / Lead X | Senior Backend Engineer, Principal Database Architect |
| **Mid IC** | X Engineer / X Designer / X Specialist | Frontend Engineer, Brand Designer |
| **Junior** | Junior X | Junior Copywriter |

**Pod rename (kill "Pod A/B/C"):**
- Stack A (Next.js + Supabase SaaS) → **Web Platform Team**
- Stack B (Shopify Native embedded) → **Embedded Apps Team**
- Stack C (Shopify External standalone) → **Storefront Apps Team**

---

## Full Title Mutation Map (45 agents)

### Executive (1)

| rex | Commander | **Chief Executive Officer** |

**Naming conflict resolution:** "CRO" is overloaded — Chief Revenue Officer vs. Conversion Rate Optimization. We have no revenue role, so **nova = Chief Research Officer** keeps the CRO acronym, and **catalyst = Director of Conversion Optimization** drops the "CRO" abbreviation entirely to avoid clash.

---

## Files to Modify

### Primary source of truth (1 file, drives the org chart UI)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/org/registry.json` — mutate `agents[<id>].title` for all 45 agents

### Agent definition files (44 files)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/*.md` — update YAML frontmatter `title:` field per the table above

### Documentation prose
- `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — replace "VP Engineering / VP Research / VP Growth / VP Creative / Head of People / CRO Lead / Pod A Lead / Pod B Lead / Pod C Lead" prose mentions with new titles. Update the agent roster table column "Use when" preamble.
- `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/memory/patterns/good/org-structure-v2.md` — replace prose-level title references (lines noted in exploration: 42, 98, 103, 125, 130, 147, 159) and rename pod-a / pod-b / pod-c sub-departments cosmetically (the IDs stay; only the human-readable label changes).

### Optional — UI label only (no schema change)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx` — change the section header strings "SaaS Stack A" / "Shopify App" / etc. to "Web Platform Team" / "Embedded Apps Team" / "Storefront Apps Team". Department badges already render `title` from registry.json so they update automatically.

---

## Execution Sequence

1. **Update `registry.json`** — single in-place edit with all 45 `title` mutations (atomic JSON write).
2. **Update agent `.md` frontmatter** — 44 small Edits, one per file, `title:` line only.
3. **Update `CLAUDE.md` prose** — search-replace VP/Pod/Stack mentions.
4. **Update `org-structure-v2.md`** — rewrite prose section headers + sub-dept labels.
5. **Update `OrgChart.tsx` section headers** — three string replacements for team labels.
6. **Restart org-chart server / let SSE re-fetch** — UI re-renders live from registry.

No registry schema change. No agent `id` change. No `department` / `subDepartment` / `reportsTo` / `pod` field change. Only display strings.

---

## Verification

1. Open `/api/org-chart` endpoint in browser — confirm new titles in JSON response.
2. Reload OrgChart UI — confirm every agent box shows the new corporate title (CEO / CTO / CDO / CMO / CGO / CRO / CPO at the top, Head of / Director of layer below, Senior/Lead/Engineer at IC layer).
3. Confirm "Pod A / Pod B / Pod C" labels are gone from team section headers.
4. Spot-check 3 agents (rex, arya, koda) by reading their `.md` frontmatter and registry.json entry — both must match.
5. `grep -r "VP Engineering\|Pod A Lead\|Pod B Lead\|Pod C Lead\|Stack A Backend\|VP Growth\|VP Research\|VP Creative" ~/.claude/` — should return no matches in active files (archives OK).
6. Confirm dispatcher agents (Rex, Arya) still route correctly — routing uses agent `id`, not `title`, so behavior is unchanged.

---

## Risks / Non-Issues

- **Routing safe:** every agent reference in dispatch logic uses `id` (e.g. `koda`, `arya`), not `title`. Renames are display-only.
- **HR cycles safe:** Cadence's promotion logic uses `level` / `tier` / `status`, not `title`.
- **Acronym clash:** resolved above (nova = Chief Research Officer; catalyst drops CRO).
- **No data migration:** zero schema change, zero ID change.

    if not f.exists():
        missing.append(aid)
        continue
    text = f.read_text()
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        continue
    end = text.find("\n---", 4)
    fm = text[:end]
    body = text[end:]

    new_name_value = f"{codename_for(aid)} — {new_title}"

    def name_replacer(m):
        prefix = m.group(1)              # 'name: ' or 'name: "'
        emoji = m.group(2).rstrip()      # emoji including any escape
        suffix = m.group(4) or ''
        # Restore original quoting
        opens_quote = prefix.rstrip().endswith('"')
        if opens_quote:
            return f'{prefix}{emoji} {new_name_value}"'
        else:
            return f'{prefix}{emoji} {new_name_value}'

    new_fm, n = name_re.subn(name_replacer, fm, count=1)
    if n == 0:
        # fallback: rewrite simpler — replace whole line
        line_re = re.compile(r'^(name:\s*).*$', re.MULTILINE)
        new_fm = line_re.sub(rf'\g<1>{new_name_value}', fm, count=1)

    # prose replacements in description/body
    new_body = body
    new_fm2 = new_fm
    for old, new in prose_repl:
        new_fm2 = new_fm2.replace(old, new)
        new_body = new_body.replace(old, new)

    f.write_text(new_fm2 + new_body)
    updated.append(aid)

print(f"Updated: {len(updated)}")
print(f"Missing: {missing}")
PY

## Report: Position Lock Feature Integration Map

### 1. **Auto-adjust Layout Button** — Line 2520-2569
- **File:line**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx:2520-2540`
- **Click handler**: Anonymous async function at line 2521
- **Function called**: `resetOrgChartPositions()` (line 2527) via lazy import from `../lib/api`
- **What it mutates**: 
  - Calls `resetOrgChartPositions()` which DELETEs only unlocked positions from the server (lines 2525-2528)
  - Reloads `positionOverrides` state via `reloadPositions()` (line 2531)
  - Sets `edges` back to `initialEdges` (line 2538)
  - Server-side deletion respects locked entries (DELETE only clears `locked: false` rows)

### 2. **Position Computation** — Deterministic + Stored State
- **Layout strategy**: Positions are **computed deterministically** from org hierarchy each render via `computeDepartmentLayout()` (line 2220)
- **Position storage**: Stored **in-memory state** + **server database** (NOT localStorage, NOT registry.json)
  - **State**: `positionOverrides` at line 2205 — `Record<string, { x: number; y: number; locked: boolean }>`
  - **Server persistence**: `/org-chart/positions` endpoint (GET/POST/DELETE)
  - **Load on mount**: `reloadPositions()` at line 2206 fetches server positions via `getOrgChartPositions()` 
  - **Overlay pattern** (line 2227-2239): Raw computed nodes overlaid with `positionOverrides` (x, y, locked flag)

### 3. **Drag-and-Drop Support** — Full Manual Positioning
- **Yes, cards are draggable** (line 2481: `nodesDraggable`)
- **Drag position persistence** (lines 2461-2478):
  - `onNodeDragStop` handler saves position to server via `saveOrgChartPositions()`
  - Updates local `positionOverrides` state with `locked: prev[node.id]?.locked ?? false` (preserves lock flag)
- **Non-draggable when locked**: Line 2235 — `draggable: !o.locked` (locked nodes get `draggable=false`)
- **Plug-in point for manual positions**: Already wired up — dragged positions auto-save to `/org-chart/positions` POST endpoint

### 4. **Per-Card Render** — Individual Agent Card
- **Leadership card (tree root)**: Line 773-875
  - `OrgLeaderNode()` component renders white card with avatar, name, title, badges
  - **No lock icon** on card itself (yet)
  - Full card is a button (line 783-867) that triggers selection via context
  
- **Department/Member card rows**: Line 992-1070 (`renderMemberRow()`)
  - Member rows rendered as buttons (line 1017-1066) inside department nodes
  - **No lock icon** on individual member cards either
  - Both use `OrgSelectContext` to trigger detail panel
  
- **Lock icon location**: Currently **only in Detail Panel** (line 2012-2031)
  - Lines 2012-2014: Lock icon badge in header when `locked===true`
  - Lines 2021-2033: Toggle lock button (Lock/Unlock icons, handler at line 2602)

### 5. **State Management** — Context + Zustand hybrid
- **Framework**: React Context (not Zustand)
  - `OrgSelectContext` (line 67-70): manages `selectedId` string + `onSelect(id)` callback
  - `positionOverrides` state (line 2205): local `useState` in `TreeViewInner` component
  - Position loading (line 2206-2217): `useCallback` + `useEffect` pattern
- **Lock state belongs**: In `positionOverrides[nodeId].locked` (boolean flag, line 2205, 2212)

### 6. **Persistence Options** — Server-First, No localStorage
- **API endpoints** (lib/api.ts:943-963):
  - `GET /org-chart/positions` — fetches all saved positions + lock state
  - `POST /org-chart/positions` — saves positions array `[{nodeId, x, y}]`
  - `DELETE /org-chart/positions[?includeLocked=1]` — clears unlocked positions (or all if flag set)
  - `POST /org-chart/positions/{nodeId}/lock` — toggle lock for one node
- **No localStorage**: No helpers found; positions live in server DB only
- **Ready-to-use PUT endpoint**: N/A — uses POST for individual saves + DELETE for batch clear

### 7. **Existing Lock UI** — Detail Panel Header
- **File:line**: `OrgChart.tsx:2012-2031`
- **Lock control today**: Toggles `locked` boolean per node via `onToggleLock` callback
  - Line 2024: title shows lock/unlock intent
  - Line 2026: button className conditionally shows amber highlight when locked
  - Line 2031: renders `Lock` (locked) or `Unlock` (unlocked) icon
- **What it does**: 
  - Calls `toggleOrgChartLock(selectedNodeData.id, next)` (line 2615)
  - If locking a node with no prior saved position, auto-saves current position first (line 2609-2613)
  - Reloads positions, updates state, shows toast feedback (line 2616-2617)

---

**Key Design Insight**: The feature is **90% built**. Lock state is already persisted per card, respects auto-adjust logic (locked cards survive reset), and toggles via the detail panel. To add **per-card lock buttons**: render a small lock/unlock button on `OrgLeaderNode` (line 788 card area) and `renderMemberRow` (line 1017 button area), wired to the same `onToggleLock` callback passed to detail panel.

91	
92	**Flow:** Roster detects gap → Forge auto-deploys to Probation → Cadence reviews in weekly cycle

95	1. Review new Probation agents in the weekly review

97	3. After 10 runs (flagged by Witness), decide: promote to Active or extend probation
98	4. If agent consistently underperforms after 20 runs: retire via Forge

102	### Hiring Rules
103	
104	1. **Train first, hire second.** If any Active/Expert agent has the skill at >= 0.4, route to Tutor for targeted training. Only hire when truly no one has signal.
105	2. **Honor the org chart.** New hire must have a clear manager. No orphans.
106	3. **Always probationary.** Every new agent starts at `level: 1 (Probation)`, `status: 'deployed'`.
107	4. **Forge proposes, you approve.** Forge generates template → you review → INSERT entry to `agents` table.
108	5. **Never hire for one-off.** If needed once, have a senior agent (level 3+) handle with elevated context.

115	3. INSERT event to `agent_events` with type='agent_created'

117	## Adaptive Promotion Logic (REPLACES Fixed Thresholds)
118	
119	You promote when:
120	
121	**Criteria (ALL must be true):**
122	1. Agent's 14-day avg composite score > peer average (same level)
123	2. Minimum 5 runs in evaluation period (query `agent_config` for `promotion_min_runs_for_review`)
124	3. No active PIP (query `agent_pips_active` for agent's id)
125	4. No Yash overrides in last 7 days (query `agent_overrides`)
126	5. No ANTIPATTERN classifications in last 30 days (query `agent_runs` WHERE `classification='ANTIPATTERN'` AND `created_at >= now() - interval '30 days'`)
127	6. (For level 3→4 only) Agent has contributed ≥1 pattern to `patterns/good/` (query `agent_contributions`)
128	
129	**Why adaptive?** No magic numbers. Each level has different peer averages. An agent is promoted when they **consistently outperform their peers**, not when they hit an arbitrary threshold.
130	
131	Examples:
132	- Active agents averaging 82 globally → peer avg = 80 → Agent at 85 = promotable ✓
133	- Expert agents averaging 88 globally → peer avg = 87 → Agent at 85 = wait, below peer avg ✗
134	- Probation agents: first 5 runs watched by Witness → auto-promote to Active if ≥3 SUCCESS + no FAILURE

136	### Implementation (In-Agent Logic)
137	
138	```sql
139	-- should_promote(agent_id)
140	SELECT CASE 
141	  WHEN acs.composite_score > peer_avg
142	    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agent_runs WHERE agent_id=$1 AND created_at >= now() - interval '14 days') >= 5
143	    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agent_pips_active WHERE agent_id=$1)
144	    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agent_overrides WHERE agent_id=$1 AND created_at >= now() - interval '7 days')
145	    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agent_runs WHERE agent_id=$1 AND classification='ANTIPATTERN' AND created_at >= now() - interval '30 days')
146	  THEN true 
147	  ELSE false 
148	END AS eligible_for_promotion
149	FROM agent_composite_scores acs
150	WHERE acs.agent_id = $1;
151	```
